'''Matija Strlič''' (born 1968) is a Slovenian heritage scientist and analytical chemist. He is Professor of Analytical Chemistry at the [[University of Ljubljana]] and Honorary Professor of [[Heritage Science]] at [[University College London]] (UCL).<ref name="About Us">{{cite web
 |title=About Us
 |url=https://hslab.fkkt.uni-lj.si/about-us/
 |website=Heritage Science Laboratory Ljubljana, University of Ljubljana
 |access-date=16 September 2026
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |title=People at the Institute for Sustainable Heritage
 |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/environment-energy-resources/heritage/people-institute-sustainable-heritage
 |website=University College London
 |access-date=16 September 2026
}}</ref>

His research focuses on the application of scientific methods to cultural heritage, including studies of degradation of historic paper and other heritage materials, effects of the environment and climate on collections, heritage values and the study of historical odours.<ref name="About Us" /><ref name="Notman">{{cite web
 |last=Notman
 |first=Nina
 |date=16 January 2023
 |title=The smell of history
 |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/features/the-smell-of-history/4016790.article
 |work=Chemistry World
 |access-date=16 September 2026
}}</ref>

Strlič studied chemistry at the [[University of Ljubljana]] and received a PhD in chemistry from the university in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof Matija Strlic |url=https://veiv.cs.ucl.ac.uk/people/academic-supervisors/72-people/academic-supervisors/159-prof-matija-strlic.html |access-date=16 September 2026 |website=University College London}}</ref>

He joined [[University College London]] in 2007 and worked at UCL's Institute for Sustainable Heritage. In 2010, Strlič was course director of UCL's newly established MRes programme in Heritage Science.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=New Masters in Heritage Science at UCL Centre for Sustainable Heritage
 |url=https://cool.culturalheritage.org/byform/mailing-lists/cdl/2010/0248.html
 |website=Conservation DistList
 |date=4 March 2010
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref> He was a co-investigator on the Science and Engineering in Arts, Heritage and Archaeology (SEAHA) Centre for Doctoral Training, an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]]-funded centre established at [[University College London]] in partnership with the [[University of Oxford]] and the [[University of Brighton]].<ref name="SEAHAlaunch">{{cite web
 |last=Terras
 |first=Melissa
 |title=Announcing SEAHA – Centre for Doctoral Training in Science and Engineering in Arts, Heritage and Archaeology
 |url=https://blogs.ucl.ac.uk/dh/2013/11/22/announcing-seaha-centre-for-doctoral-training-in-science-and-engineering-in-arts-heritage-and-archaeology/
 |website=UCL Digital Humanities
 |publisher=University College London
 |date=22 November 2013
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref> He was also a member of the SEAHA Steering Committee.<ref name="SEAHA">{{cite conference
 |title=2nd International SEAHA Conference: Book of Abstracts
 |location=Oxford, UK
 |date=20–21 June 2016
 |publisher=University College London
 |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/sites/bartlett/files/2025-05/2016_seaha_conference_book_of_abstracts.pdf
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref> He was Deputy Director of UCL Institute for Sustainable Heritage until 2019.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Matija Strlic – About
 |url=https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/8768-matija-strlic/about
 |website=University College London
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref>

He also taught on the MSc in Conservation for Archaeology and Museums at UCL Institute of Archaeology (2008-2019).<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Matija Strlic – Teaching
 |url=https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/8768-matija-strlic/teaching
 |website=University College London
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref>

Strlič served as a Senior Research Fellow at the Smithsonian Institution's Museum Conservation Institute between 2020 and 2022.<ref name="Columbia Smithsonian">{{cite web
|title=Good pollution: Smells in museums
|url=https://www.arch.columbia.edu/events/2262-good-pollution-smells-in-museums
|website=Columbia University Graduate School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation
|date=8 April 2021
|access-date=20 September 2026
}}</ref>

At the University of Ljubljana, Strlič is Professor of Analytical Chemistry and leads the Heritage Science Laboratory Ljubljana.<ref name="About Us" /> He is listed among the teaching staff of the Chair of Analytical Chemistry,<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Chair of Analytical Chemistry
 |url=https://fkkt.uni-lj.si/en/organization/department-of-chemistry-and-biochemistry/chair-of-analytical-chemistry
 |website=University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Technology
 |access-date=19 September 2026
}}</ref> where he has taught courses in Analytical chemistry (since 1997) and Natural sciences for conservators (since 2019).

He heads the Centre of Excellence in Green [[Heritage Science]],<ref name="GreenHerAbout">GreenHer CoE, "[https://greenher.uni-lj.si/about-us/ About us]", University of Ljubljana. Accessed 19 September 2026.</ref> an interinstitutional Centre established in Slovenia and funded by the [[European Commission]] through the Teaming instrument of the Widening programme.<ref name="CORDIS GreenHer">European Commission, "[https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101136457 GreenHer Centre of Excellence: Green Heritage Science]", ''CORDIS'', grant agreement No. 101136457, 2025.</ref>

He is member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]<ref name="EASA Strlič">European Academy of Sciences and Arts, "[https://euro-acad.eu/fileGreetings.php?path=JcjqsJxxDEVPYnM7ciBE New Members Elected by the Senate]", 2024.</ref> and is Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and the [[International Institute for Conservation of Historic and Artistic Works]]. Strlič has been included in the [[Stanford University|Stanford]]–Elsevier list of the world's top 2% of scientists,<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Top 2% Scientists
 |url=https://www.topscinet.com/university_profile/Univerza%20v%20Ljubljani/?name=Univerza+v+Ljubljani&stype=single_year
 |website=TOPSCINET
 |access-date=21 September 2026
}}</ref> and his [[Scopus]] author profile records more than 190 publications.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Author details: Strlic, Matija
 |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7004705339
 |website=Scopus
 |access-date=21 September 2026
}}</ref>

In 2002, Strlič received the Zois award for outstanding scientific contributions in chemistry,<ref>{{cite web |title=Nagrade in priznanja za izjemne dosežke v znanstveno-raziskovalni in razvojni dejavnosti – 2002 |url=http://mizs.arhiv-spletisc.gov.si/si/delovna_podrocja/direktorat_za_znanost/sektor_za_znanost/dejavnost/nagrade_in_priznanja_za_izjemne_dosezke_v_znanstveno_raziskovalni_in_razvojni_dejavnosti/2002/index.html |website=Ministrstvo za šolstvo, znanost in šport |language=sl |access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref> and in 2015, he received the Ambassador of Science of the Republic of Slovenia Award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nagrade in priznanja za izjemne dosežke v znanstveno-raziskovalni in razvojni dejavnosti – 2015 |url=http://mizs.arhiv-spletisc.gov.si/si/delovna_podrocja/direktorat_za_znanost/sektor_za_znanost/dejavnost/nagrade_in_priznanja_za_izjemne_dosezke_v_znanstveno_raziskovalni_in_razvojni_dejavnosti/2015/index.html |website=Ministrstvo za izobraževanje, znanost in šport |language=sl |access-date=19 September 2026}}</ref> In 2026, Strlič received the Research Collaboration Index Arts & Humanities Subject Award in recognition of his highly collaborative and cross-disciplinary research.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arts & Humanities Subject Award |website=Research Collaboration Index |url=https://www.globalresearchpartnerships.com/rci/awards/arts-humanities/ |access-date=4 October 2026}}</ref>
